sections.title: Letter sound
paragraphs: The name of this letter sounds like (я) /ja/. Its main sound is heard in (яблоко) /ˈja.blə.kə/, which means apple. This letter makes four sounds in spoken Russian.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, lift the middle of your tongue near the roof of your mouth. Then open your jaw wide. For the second sound, drop your jaw wide with your tongue low. For the third, start near the roof and open slightly. For the fourth, raise your tongue high and forward. Place a hand on your throat. Your vocal cords must vibrate for all four sounds.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: At the start of a word or after another vowel, a stressed syllable sounds like (я) /ja/. You also hear this sound in (маяк) /mɐˈjak/. After a palatalized consonant under stress, the vowel sounds like (мясо) /ˈmʲa.sə/ or (пять) /pʲatʲ/. Without stress, at the start of a word it sounds like (яйцо) /jɪjˈt͡so/ or (пояс) /ˈpo.jɪs/. Finally, after a palatalized consonant in an unstressed syllable before stress, it sounds like (мясной) /mʲɪsˈnoj/ or (тянуть) /tʲɪˈnutʲ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pronounce the unstressed vowel as a clear ah sound like father. In unstressed syllables, keep the sound short and close to the short i in sit. When the letter stands after a consonant, do not insert a separate y sound like in yard. Instead, soften the consonant itself and glide directly into the vowel.
